entries.title: Heartbeat apply semantics contradict P3
entries.description: The spec says the heartbeat job only checks and writes notification records, never applies updates, and autonomous apply is not in v1. P3 exit criteria then require ten stable customer installs to auto-apply a migration on their next heartbeat-driven check. Those cannot both be true, and this ambiguity affects the core automation path.

entries.title: Telemetry opt-in is not actually opt-in
entries.description: The Vision says telemetry is opt-in by channel, but the channel table says stable telemetry is opt-in with default ON. Customer installs also default to stable, which means a new customer install may phone home unless a user opts out. That is not opt-in under an adversarial reading and conflicts with the privacy posture.

entries.title: Agent rule and config changes are not gated
entries.description: The risky-change list gates executables, hooks, MCP configs, and permission grants, but omits agent instructions, rules, skills, schemas, prompts, and behavior-driving registries. In this repository, non-executable text files can materially change agent behavior and customer-visible outcomes. A malicious or mistaken safe_additive update could alter behavior without tripping the explicit approval categories.

entries.title: Unsigned manifests can still drive v1 auto-apply
entries.description: The architecture opens by saying installs read a signed manifest, but the phases make signing checksum-only in P1 and warn-only in P3/v1. Since stable customer roots can auto-apply safe_additive updates, an attacker who controls or tampers with the manifest source can still cause changes while signature verification is non-enforcing. Checksums inside the manifest do not protect against a compromised manifest.

entries.title: Rollback for additive new files is underspecified
entries.description: Rollback guarantees restoring every file in manifest.sha256.json to its pre-apply SHA, but additive updates may create files that had no pre-apply SHA. The spec also says rollback must not delete operator-created work unless the file was explicitly generated by the update. Without a tombstone or pre-state marker, rollback cannot distinguish update-created files from user-created files at the same path after a crash or partial apply.

entries.title: Customer approval artifacts lack freshness rules
entries.description: Permits in UPDATE_POLICY.md and approval tokens satisfy risky updates, but the spec only says doctor warns on stale permits. It does not define expiry, replay protection, token versioning, or whether a permit remains valid after a migration changes contents but keeps the same id. This weakens approval from an intentional per-change gate into a potentially permanent bypass.

entries.title: Approved migrations cannot autoapply
entries.description: The spec now says P3 customer installs with autonomous_apply true apply an approved migration through the autoapply job. But the autoapply job is constrained so every PlanItem must evaluate to AUTO_APPLY, and any REQUIRES_APPROVAL refuses the whole apply. Risky migrations are defined to produce REQUIRES_APPROVAL unless approved, so a valid approval token still cannot satisfy the autoapply path as written.

entries.title: P1 approval-token happy path conflicts with deferred signatures
entries.description: P1 exit criteria require a matching-token APPROVED_APPLY happy path on a rule_change item, but P1 also says signature verification is stubbed and signed TrustEvidence is not yet possible. The approval artifact contract says tokens require ed25519 signatures and invalid or missing signatures are BLOCKED. As written, P1 cannot both satisfy the token happy path and preserve the approval contract unless it implements token verification earlier or uses a different approval artifact kind.
